div.head: Chapter 7
div.p: The sole and final cause for the Apostolic See granting the supreme principality and imperial superiority over that new world of the Indies to the kings of Castile and León, was the preaching of the Gospel and the spreading of the Christian faith and religion and the conversion of those peoples native to it, and not in order to make them greater lords or richer princes than they already were.

This principle is proved. First, because for the Supreme Pontiff to involve himself in exercising jurisdiction and his power in disposing of the temporal affairs of laypeople, he is not accustomed to do so without a true, examined, and necessary cause. And this even within the universal Church among Christians, of whom we are all his subjects in spiritual matters; and in a certain case and with cause, in temporal matters as well. All of this is made plain by the theologians in the Sentences 2 d. 44, and in particular Thomas 2.2 q. 88 a. 11 and 12, and in De regimine principum, lib. 3, c. 13 and Henry of Ghent, Quodlibeta, IV et VI, Augustinus of Ancona, Lib. De potestate Pape, q. 23 a. 2 et 3, Peter of Palude, Lib. De potestate Pape, and other doctors in various treatises that they wrote on the subject, and by the canonists in cap. novit, De indiciis; et in cap. per venerabilem, Extra, Qui filii sint legitimi, et in cap. que in ecclesiarum, De Constitutionibus, and by the civil lawyers in L. fin., Codex, Si contra ius et utilitatem publicam.

Now the kingdoms and peoples of that world, belonging as they do to the fourth category of unbelievers and standing outside the universal Church, are subjects of it neither in spiritual nor in temporal matters, nor of any member of it, because they hold no foreign lands or kingdoms, nor have they done harm to the Church or its members, nor impeded the faith, whether by domicile or by contract or by any other cause of subjection, but are entirely free; therefore, still less would the vicar of Christ involve himself, or have involved himself, in disposing of the temporal goods of those and like unbelievers without a true, examined, and necessary cause. For there was and could have been no cause in law that was true and just, given all that has been said above, save the preaching of the faith and the conversion of those same peoples, as is self-evident. Therefore, the sole and final cause for the Apostolic See granting the supreme principality and superiority over that new world of the Indies to the kings of Castile and León, was the preaching of the Gospel and the spreading of the faith and the conversion of those peoples, etc.

Secondly, the third principle is proved by the express words of the very supreme pontiff Alexander VI himself, who made the said concession, who says the following: "desiring that the name of our Savior be brought to those parts, we exhort you greatly in the Lord, by the reception of the holy baptism by which you are bound to the apostolic commandments, and with all the fervor of the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ we earnestly require of you, that when with prompt spirit and with zeal for the orthodox faith you are prepared to pursue and undertake this enterprise entirely, you are willing and must induce the peoples of the said islands and lands to embrace the Christian religion, etc." And that this is the sole and final cause, see the Tractado Comprobatorio del Derecho que tienen los Reyes de Castilla y León en las Indias, in the final proof of the first conclusion, where it will be found copiously demonstrated. Therefore, the sole and final cause for the Apostolic See granting it, etc., was the preaching of the Gospel and the spreading of the faith and the conversion of those peoples, etc.
